<div class="alert alert-info">

# Purpose {.unnumbered .unlisted}

Code each song as a sequence of 5 ms segments, each in one of 5 states, so that songs can be aligned and compared.

</div>

&nbsp;

# Load packages {.unnumbered .unlisted}

```{r load packages, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

sketchy::load_packages(packages = c("knitr", "Rraven", "ggplot2", "viridis", "tuneR", "seewave", "mclust"))

theme_set(theme_classic(base_size = 13))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, dpi = 120, fig.retina = 1)

states <- c("D", "P", "U", "F", "S")
state_names <- c("D: descending tone", "P: flat tone", "U: ascending tone", "F: fast trill", "S: slow trill")
cat_cols <- setNames(viridis(5, option = "H", begin = 0.05, end = 0.95), states)
txt_col <- setNames(c("white", "black", "black", "black", "white"), states)
broad_cols <- c(tone = "#4C78A8", trill = "#B279A2")

# parameters of the coding
segment_ms <- 5              # duration of the segments
trill_cut_ms <- 13           # fast < 13 ms <= slow
tone_cut <- 14               # D < -14 kHz/s <= P < 14 kHz/s <= U
tone_window_ms <- 5          # slope measured on the segment +- 5 ms (15 ms in total)

```

# The procedure

The goal is to turn each song into a string of letters, one letter per `r segment_ms` ms of song. Each letter is one of five states, two for trills and three for pure tones:

| State | Sound | Rule |
|:---|:-----|:-----|
| **F** | fast trill | trill period < `r trill_cut_ms` ms |
| **S** | slow trill | trill period ≥ `r trill_cut_ms` ms |
| **D** | descending tone | frequency slope < `r -tone_cut` kHz/s |
| **P** | flat tone | frequency slope from `r -tone_cut` to `r tone_cut` kHz/s |
| **U** | ascending tone | frequency slope ≥ `r tone_cut` kHz/s |

The **trill period** is the duration of one oscillation cycle of the frequency contour. The **frequency slope** is how fast the frequency changes over time. Both are measured on the frequency contour of each song. Contours were extracted as dominant frequency contours with the function `freq_ts()` from the warbleR package and then manually tailored where needed. Apart from this tailoring, only the first step is done by hand. The rest follows from fixed rules.

The coding has four steps:

1. **Divide the song into broad sections (manual).** A person marks where each section starts and ends, and labels it as pure tone or trill. Consecutive pure tone sections are merged. Trills that differ discretely in rate are annotated as separate sections.
2. **Classify the trills.** The trill period of each whole trill section is measured, and the section is assigned to fast (F) or slow (S).
3. **Split the song into `r segment_ms` ms segments.** The whole song is split, tones and trills alike. Each trill segment takes the state of its section. Tone segments have no state yet.
4. **Classify the tones.** The frequency slope around each tone segment is measured, and the segment is assigned to descending (D), flat (P) or ascending (U).

The order of the steps follows from the two kinds of sound:

- **Trills are classified before splitting** because one trill cycle lasts about 10 - 20 ms, so a `r segment_ms` ms segment contains only part of a cycle and its period cannot be measured.
- **Tones are classified after splitting** because the frequency of a single tone section can fall and then rise. Classifying each segment captures those changes, which a single label for the whole section would miss.

For example, a song that starts with a descending tone followed by a slow trill could be coded as `dddddssssssss`. Because segments have a fixed duration, longer sounds produce more letters, and songs can differ in sequence length.

The same five example songs are shown after each step, with the output of that step overlaid on the spectrogram.

# Step 1: manual broad sections

Each song was manually divided into consecutive sections, each labelled as **pure tone** or **trill**. Consecutive pure tone sections are merged into a single section. Consecutive trill sections are not merged: the rate of trills did not seem to vary gradually but rather discretely, so when discrete variation was observed the trills were annotated individually. The start and end of each song come from its tailored frequency contour. Sections annotated with the wrong song are reassigned to the song whose contour contains them.

```{r read data}

contours <- read.csv("./data/raw/segment_classification/seltailor_output.csv")
ff_cols <- grep("^ff", names(contours))

segs <- imp_raven(path = "./data/raw/segment_classification", files = "FrameworkContourDegradationv1.7.txt",
                  all.data = TRUE, warbler.format = TRUE)
segs <- segs[!is.na(segs$Category) & segs$Category != "" & segs$ID %in% contours$song.type, ]

# reassign segments annotated with the wrong song
tol <- 0.005
m <- match(segs$ID, contours$song.type)
outside <- segs$end < contours$start[m] - tol | segs$start > contours$end[m] + tol
segs$ID[outside] <- vapply(which(outside), function(i) {
  k <- which(contours$start <= segs$start[i] + tol & contours$end >= segs$end[i] - tol)
  if (length(k) == 1) contours$song.type[k] else NA_character_
}, character(1))
segs <- segs[!is.na(segs$ID), ]
segs <- segs[order(segs$ID, segs$start), ]

# broad class of each section
segs$class <- ifelse(segs$Category %in% c("F", "M", "S"), "trill", "tone")

# merge consecutive pure tone sections (trill sections are kept as annotated)
n <- nrow(segs)
new_section <- c(TRUE, segs$ID[-1] != segs$ID[-n] | segs$class[-1] != "tone" | segs$class[-n] != "tone")
merged_end <- as.vector(tapply(segs$end, cumsum(new_section), max))
segs <- segs[new_section, ]
segs$end <- merged_end

segs$lek.song.type <- sub("-[0-9]{4}$", "", sub("^[0-9]+-", "", segs$ID))
segs$lek <- sub("-.*", "", segs$lek.song.type)
segs$duration_ms <- (segs$end - segs$start) * 1000

data.frame(recordings = length(unique(segs$ID)), song_types = length(unique(segs$lek.song.type)), sections = nrow(segs))
data.frame(class = c("tone", "trill"), sections = as.vector(table(segs$class)),
           median_duration_ms = round(as.vector(tapply(segs$duration_ms, segs$class, median)), 1))

# contour of each recording
CT <- lapply(split(contours, contours$song.type), function(ct)
  list(t = seq(ct$start, ct$end, length.out = length(ff_cols)), f = unlist(ct[, ff_cols]), start = ct$start, end = ct$end))

# slope (kHz/s) and trill period (ms) of the contour in a time window
measure <- function(id, a, b) {
  k <- CT[[id]]
  n <- max(8, sum(k$t >= a & k$t <= b))
  ti <- seq(a, b, length.out = n)
  fi <- approx(k$t, k$f, xout = ti, rule = 2)$y
  d1 <- diff(fi); sg <- sign(d1[abs(d1) > 0.05])
  n_ext <- if (length(sg) > 1) sum(diff(sg) != 0) else 0
  osc <- n_ext / 2 / (b - a)
  c(slope = unname(coef(lm(fi ~ ti))[2]), period_ms = if (osc > 0) 1000 / osc else Inf)
}

```

## Output of step 1

```{r plotting functions}

wave <- readWave("./data/raw/segment_classification/contour-degradation_325_songs.wav")
sr <- wave@samp.rate

# example songs shown after each step
examples <- c("7-BR1-C1-2012", "58-CCE-I2-2012", "109-HC1-F2-1992", "209-SUR-B1-1972", "303-TR1-E3-2012")

strip_names <- c("broad sections", "trills classified", "5 ms segments", "5 ms states")

# blocks (start, end, color, label) available after each step
step_output <- function(id, step) {
  if (step <= 2) {
    d <- segs[segs$ID == id, ]
    tr <- d$class == "trill"
    if (step == 1) return(data.frame(start = d$start, end = d$end, fill = broad_cols[d$class], txt = "white", label = d$class, cex = 0.8))
    lab <- ifelse(tr, ifelse(is.finite(d$period_ms), sprintf("%s (%.1f ms)", d$trill_state, d$period_ms), d$trill_state), "tone")
    return(data.frame(start = d$start, end = d$end, fill = ifelse(tr, cat_cols[d$trill_state], broad_cols["tone"]),
                      txt = ifelse(tr, txt_col[d$trill_state], "white"), label = lab, cex = 0.8))
  }
  z <- P[P$ID == id, ]; z <- z[order(z$segment), ]
  if (step == 3) {
    tr <- z$class == "trill"
    return(data.frame(start = z$start, end = z$end, fill = ifelse(tr, cat_cols[z$trill_state], broad_cols["tone"]),
                      txt = ifelse(tr, txt_col[z$trill_state], "white"), label = ifelse(tr, z$trill_state, ""), cex = 0.55))
  }
  data.frame(start = z$start, end = z$end, fill = cat_cols[z$state], txt = txt_col[z$state], label = z$state, cex = 0.55)
}

# all spectrograms share the same time range (longest song of the five leks plus margins),
# so that segments have the same size in all plots
time_range_ms <- 210

# spectrogram with the output of a step overlaid and shown as labelled strip(s) on top
plot_step <- function(id, steps, margin = 0.008, flim = c(1, 11)) {
  k <- CT[[id]]
  t0 <- max(0, k$start - margin); t1 <- k$end + margin
  sp <- spectro(cutw(wave, f = sr, from = t0, to = t1, output = "Wave"), f = sr, wl = 256, ovlp = 90, plot = FALSE, flim = c(0, 13))
  amp <- sp$amp; amp[amp < -45] <- -45
  tms <- sp$time * 1000; ms <- function(x) (x - t0) * 1000

  h <- 1.2; top <- flim[2] + length(steps) * h
  par(mar = c(3.3, 7, 2, 0.5))
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, time_range_ms), ylim = c(flim[1], top), xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i", xlab = "", ylab = "", yaxt = "n", main = id, cex.main = 0.95)
  mtext("Time (ms)", side = 1, line = 2.1, cex = 0.8)
  axis(2, at = seq(ceiling(flim[1]), flim[2], 2), las = 1, cex.axis = 0.8)
  mtext("kHz", side = 2, line = 2.2, at = mean(flim), cex = 0.8)
  fsel <- sp$freq >= flim[1] & sp$freq <= flim[2]
  image(tms, sp$freq[fsel], t(amp[fsel, ]), col = gray.colors(40, start = 1, end = 0), add = TRUE, useRaster = TRUE)

  # overlay of the last step
  o <- step_output(id, tail(steps, 1))
  rect(ms(o$start), flim[1], ms(o$end), flim[2], col = adjustcolor(o$fill, 0.33), border = NA)
  segments(ms(c(o$start, tail(o$end, 1))), flim[1], y1 = flim[2], col = "gray25", lwd = 0.5)
  lines(ms(k$t), k$f, col = "white", lwd = 3); lines(ms(k$t), k$f, col = "#FF8C00", lwd = 1.2)

  # labelled strips
  rect(0, flim[2], time_range_ms, top, col = "white", border = NA)
  for (i in seq_along(steps)) {
    o <- step_output(id, steps[i])
    y0 <- top - i * h
    rect(ms(o$start), y0, ms(o$end), y0 + h, col = o$fill, border = "white", lwd = 0.4)
    fits <- 1.15 * strwidth(o$label, cex = o$cex) < ms(o$end) - ms(o$start)
    text(ms((o$start + o$end) / 2), y0 + h / 2, ifelse(fits, o$label, ""), col = o$txt, cex = o$cex, font = 2)
    mtext(strip_names[steps[i]], side = 2, at = y0 + h / 2, las = 1, line = 0.3, cex = 0.65, adj = 1)
  }
  box()
}

plot_legend <- function(step) {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
  plot.new()
  fl <- switch(as.character(step),
               "1" = broad_cols, "4" = cat_cols,
               c(broad_cols["tone"], cat_cols[c("F", "S")]))
  lb <- switch(as.character(step),
               "1" = c("pure tone", "trill"), "4" = state_names,
               c("pure tone (not yet classified)", "F: fast trill", "S: slow trill"))
  legend("center", horiz = TRUE, bty = "n", fill = fl, border = NA, cex = 0.9, legend = lb)
}

plot_examples <- function(step) {
  layout(matrix(1:6), heights = c(0.45, rep(3.2, 5)))
  par(cex = 1)
  plot_legend(step)
  for (id in examples) plot_step(id, step)
}

```

Spectrograms of the five example songs with the broad sections overlaid (orange: tailored contour):

```{r step 1 output, fig.width = 10.5, fig.height = 16.45}

plot_examples(1)

```

# Step 2: classify trills

The **trill period** (ms per oscillation cycle) of each whole trill section is 1000 / oscillation rate, where the oscillation rate is half the number of direction changes of the contour per second (changes < 50 Hz ignored). A section is needed for this measurement: a 5 ms segment is much shorter than one trill cycle.

```{r trill period}

tr_idx <- which(segs$class == "trill")
segs$period_ms <- NA
segs$period_ms[tr_idx] <- mapply(function(id, a, b) measure(id, a, b)[["period_ms"]],
                                 segs$ID[tr_idx], segs$start[tr_idx], segs$end[tr_idx])
segs$trill_state <- ifelse(segs$class == "trill", ifelse(segs$period_ms < trill_cut_ms, "F", "S"), NA)

```

## Natural groups in trill period

```{r trill groups, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}

x <- segs$period_ms[tr_idx]; x <- x[is.finite(x)]
bic <- mclustBIC(x, G = 1:5, modelNames = "V", verbose = FALSE)
mod <- Mclust(x, G = which.max(bic[, "V"]), modelNames = "V", verbose = FALSE)

data.frame(groups = 1:5, BIC = round(bic[, "V"]))
data.frame(mean_ms = round(mod$parameters$mean, 1), sd_ms = round(sqrt(mod$parameters$variance$sigmasq), 1), proportion = round(mod$parameters$pro, 2))

ggplot(data.frame(x), aes(x)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.5, fill = "gray70", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = trill_cut_ms, linetype = 2) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 40)) + labs(x = "Trill period (ms)", y = "Trill sections")

```

A mixture of two groups is preferred (BIC): fast trills (~10 ms) and slow trills (~20 ms). The dashed line marks the threshold used (`r trill_cut_ms` ms), close to the point at which the two groups are equally likely.

## Output of step 2

Trill sections now have a state, shown with their trill period. Tone sections are not yet classified:

```{r step 2 output, fig.width = 10.5, fig.height = 16.45}

plot_examples(2)

```

# Step 3: split into 5 ms segments

Each whole song (tones and trills, from the start to the end of its tailored contour) is split into consecutive `r segment_ms` ms segments. A last remainder of at least half a segment forms its own (shorter) segment, and a shorter remainder is added to the previous segment. Each segment belongs to the section that covers most of it, and trill segments inherit the state of their section.

```{r split}

split_song <- function(id) {
  ii <- which(segs$ID == id); k <- CT[[id]]; d <- segment_ms / 1000
  b <- seq(k$start, k$end, by = d)
  if (k$end - b[length(b)] >= d / 2 || length(b) == 1) b <- c(b, k$end) else b[length(b)] <- k$end
  n <- length(b) - 1
  data.frame(ID = id, segment = 1:n, start = b[-(n + 1)], end = b[-1],
             section = sapply(1:n, function(j) ii[which.max(pmax(0, pmin(segs$end[ii], b[j + 1]) - pmax(segs$start[ii], b[j])))]))
}
P <- do.call(rbind, lapply(unique(segs$ID), split_song))
P$class <- segs$class[P$section]
P$trill_state <- segs$trill_state[P$section]
P$lek.song.type <- segs$lek.song.type[P$section]
P$taxon <- sub("^[0-9]+-", "", P$ID)
P$year <- as.numeric(sub(".*-", "", P$ID))

data.frame(segments = nrow(P), tone = sum(P$class == "tone"), trill = sum(P$class == "trill"))

```

## Output of step 3

All sections are now split into 5 ms segments. Trill segments carry the state of their section, and tone segments are not yet classified:

```{r step 3 output, fig.width = 10.5, fig.height = 16.45}

plot_examples(3)

```

# Step 4: classify tones

The **frequency slope** of each tone segment is measured with a linear fit to the contour in a `r 2 * tone_window_ms + segment_ms` ms window centred on the segment (kept within its section). The window reduces the effect of small irregularities of the contour while still following changes in direction within a section.

Thresholds: **D** < `r -tone_cut` kHz/s ≤ **P** < `r tone_cut` kHz/s ≤ **U**.

```{r classify tones}

to_idx <- which(P$class == "tone")
w <- tone_window_ms / 1000
P$slope <- NA
P$slope[to_idx] <- sapply(to_idx, function(i) {
  s <- P$section[i]
  a <- max(P$start[i] - w, segs$start[s]); b <- min(P$end[i] + w, segs$end[s])
  if (b - a < 0.002) { a <- segs$start[s]; b <- segs$end[s] }
  measure(P$ID[i], a, b)[["slope"]]
})

P$state <- ifelse(P$class == "trill", segs$trill_state[P$section],
                  ifelse(P$slope < -tone_cut, "D", ifelse(P$slope < tone_cut, "P", "U")))

round(prop.table(table(factor(P$state, states))), 3)

```

## Natural groups in tone slope

As with trills, the thresholds are placed where neighbouring groups of a mixture model are equally likely. The model is fitted to the absolute slope, so that the two thresholds are symmetric and a flat tone is treated the same whether it falls or rises slightly.

```{r tone groups, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}

a <- abs(sl <- P$slope[to_idx]); a <- a[a > 0 & a < 150]
tone_bic <- mclustBIC(a, G = 1:6, modelNames = "V", verbose = FALSE)
tone_mod <- Mclust(a, G = 3, modelNames = "V", verbose = FALSE)
grid <- seq(0.05, 150, by = 0.05)
tone_bound <- grid[which(diff(predict(tone_mod, grid)$classification) != 0)]

data.frame(groups = 1:6, BIC = round(tone_bic[, "V"]))
data.frame(group = c("flat", "gentle slope", "steep slope"), mean_kHz_s = round(tone_mod$parameters$mean, 1),
           sd_kHz_s = round(sqrt(tone_mod$parameters$variance$sigmasq), 1), proportion = round(tone_mod$parameters$pro, 2))
data.frame(boundaries_kHz_s = round(tone_bound, 1))

ggplot(data.frame(x = sl[abs(sl) < 150]), aes(x)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 2, fill = "gray70", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1) * tone_cut, linetype = 2) +
  labs(x = "Frequency slope (kHz/s)", y = "Tone segments")

```

The groups are less distinct than those of trills: slopes vary continuously, and BIC prefers `r which.max(tone_bic[, "V"])` groups rather than a clear small number. Three groups are used because they separate flat tones from gentle and steep slopes. The boundary between flat tones and gentle slopes (`r round(tone_bound[1], 1)` kHz/s) sets the threshold used (dashed lines, ±`r tone_cut` kHz/s). Gentle and steep slopes are both coded as ascending or descending according to their sign.

The final coding, with a state for all 5 ms segments:


# Sequences

Sequences are saved for two sets of recordings: the five leks used in the paper (BR1, CCE, HC1, SUR and TR1) and all leks. The thresholds above were set using all recordings, and the rest of this report uses the five leks.

Three tables are saved in `data/processed`, each in two versions (add `_all_leks` to the file name for the version with all leks):

- `song_5ms_segments_by_recording.csv`: all segments with their state
- `song_5ms_sequences_by_taxon.csv`: the sequence of each song type and year (one recording per song type and year)
- `song_5ms_sequences_by_song_type.csv`: one sequence per song type, from its **most representative recording** (highest mean similarity to the other recordings of the song type)

```{r sequences}

Q <- lapply(split(P, factor(P$ID, levels = unique(P$ID))), function(z) z$state[order(z$segment)])
seq_str <- sapply(Q, paste, collapse = "")

similarity <- function(a, b) 1 - adist(seq_str[[a]], seq_str[[b]])[1, 1] / max(nchar(seq_str[[a]]), nchar(seq_str[[b]]))

rec <- unique(P[, c("ID", "lek.song.type", "taxon", "year")])
rec$lek <- sub("-.*", "", rec$lek.song.type)
rec$length <- nchar(seq_str[rec$ID])
rec$sequence <- tolower(seq_str[rec$ID])

by_type <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(rec, rec$lek.song.type), function(z) {
  if (nrow(z) == 1) { best <- 1; ms <- NA } else {
    S <- outer(z$ID, z$ID, Vectorize(similarity)); diag(S) <- NA
    ms <- rowMeans(S, na.rm = TRUE); best <- which.max(ms); ms <- ms[best]
  }
  data.frame(lek = z$lek[1], song.type = z$lek.song.type[1], n_recordings = nrow(z), representative_recording = z$ID[best],
             mean_similarity_to_others = round(ms, 3), length = z$length[best], sequence = z$sequence[best])
}))

write_tables <- function(P, rec, by_type, suffix = "") {
  write.csv(P[, c("ID", "lek.song.type", "taxon", "year", "segment", "start", "end", "class", "slope", "state")],
            paste0("./data/processed/song_5ms_segments_by_recording", suffix, ".csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(rec[, c("lek", "lek.song.type", "year", "taxon", "ID", "length", "sequence")],
            paste0("./data/processed/song_5ms_sequences_by_taxon", suffix, ".csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(by_type, paste0("./data/processed/song_5ms_sequences_by_song_type", suffix, ".csv"), row.names = FALSE)
}

# all leks
write_tables(P, rec, by_type, "_all_leks")
rec_all <- rec
summary_all <- data.frame(leks = "all", recordings = nrow(rec), song_types = nrow(by_type))

# leks used in the paper
sel_leks <- c("BR1", "CCE", "HC1", "SUR", "TR1")
P <- P[sub("-.*", "", P$lek.song.type) %in% sel_leks, ]
rec <- rec[rec$lek %in% sel_leks, ]
by_type <- by_type[by_type$lek %in% sel_leks, ]
Q <- Q[rec$ID]
write_tables(P, rec, by_type)

rbind(summary_all, data.frame(leks = "used in the paper", recordings = nrow(rec), song_types = nrow(by_type)))
data.frame(taxa = nrow(rec), song_types = nrow(by_type), median_length = median(rec$length), min_length = min(rec$length), max_length = max(rec$length))
head(by_type[, c("song.type", "n_recordings", "length", "sequence")])

```

## FASTA files for alignment

FASTA files are saved in `data/processed/song_sequences_5ms`. For each lek, taxa (song type x year) are split into `early_old`, `rest_old`, `early_new`, `rest_new` and `no.fossils`.

Each set comes in two formats:

- `song_seqs_<set>_<lek>.fa`: states as lower-case letters (d, p, u, f, s), for MAFFT
- `song_seqs_<set>_<lek>_prank.fa`: nucleotide coding for PRANK: trills as pyrimidines (f = C, s = T) and tones as purines (u = A, d = G, with flat tones ambiguous between them, p = R)

Sequences of taxa are provided in two versions, in separate folders:

- `song_type_sequence`: all years of a song type share the sequence of its most representative recording
- `year_specific_sequence`: each song type and year has the sequence of its own recording. Taxa with no recording in that year use the representative sequence of the song type

`taxon_sequence_source.csv` gives the recording used for each taxon, and `all_recordings.fa` and `all_recordings_all_leks.fa` have the sequences of all recordings from the five leks and from all leks.

```{r fasta files}

out_dir <- "./data/processed/song_sequences_5ms"
for (d in c("song_type_sequence", "year_specific_sequence")) dir.create(file.path(out_dir, d), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

to_prank <- function(x) chartr("fsudp", "CTAGR", x)
write_fasta <- function(names, seqs, file) writeLines(as.vector(rbind(paste0(">", names), seqs)), file)

yrs <- read.csv("./data/raw/year_range_by_song_type.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
yrs <- yrs[yrs$lek %in% sel_leks, ]
yrs$taxon <- paste(yrs$song.type, yrs$year, sep = "-")
yrs <- yrs[order(yrs$song.type, yrs$year), ]

# sequence of each taxon
yrs$representative_recording <- by_type$representative_recording[match(yrs$song.type, by_type$song.type)]
yrs$own_recording <- rec$ID[match(yrs$taxon, rec$taxon)]
yrs$has_recording <- !is.na(yrs$own_recording)
yrs$seq_song_type <- by_type$sequence[match(yrs$song.type, by_type$song.type)]
yrs$seq_year <- ifelse(yrs$has_recording, rec$sequence[match(yrs$taxon, rec$taxon)], yrs$seq_song_type)
stopifnot(!anyNA(yrs$seq_song_type))

write.csv(data.frame(lek = yrs$lek, taxon = yrs$taxon, song.type = yrs$song.type, year = yrs$year,
                     has_recording_that_year = yrs$has_recording,
                     recording_song_type_sequence = yrs$representative_recording,
                     recording_year_specific_sequence = ifelse(yrs$has_recording, yrs$own_recording, yrs$representative_recording)),
          file.path(out_dir, "taxon_sequence_source.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write_fasta(rec$ID, rec$sequence, file.path(out_dir, "all_recordings.fa"))
write_fasta(rec_all$ID, rec_all$sequence, file.path(out_dir, "all_recordings_all_leks.fa"))

# taxon sets
all_old <- yrs
early_old <- all_old[!duplicated(all_old$song.type), ]
all_new <- all_old[all_old$year > 2000, ]
early_new <- early_old[early_old$year > 2000, ]
rest_old <- all_old[!all_old$taxon %in% early_old$taxon, ]
rest_new <- all_new[!all_new$taxon %in% early_new$taxon, ]
no_fossils <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(all_old, all_old$lek), function(z) z[z$year == max(z$year), ]))

sets <- list(early_old = early_old, rest_old = rest_old, early_new = early_new, rest_new = rest_new, no.fossils = no_fossils)
n_files <- 0
for (i in sel_leks) for (set in names(sets)) {
  z <- sets[[set]][sets[[set]]$lek == i, ]
  if (grepl("old", set) && !any(all_old$year[all_old$lek == i] < 2000)) next
  if (set == "no.fossils" && nrow(z) <= 3) next
  if (!nrow(z)) next
  for (v in c("song_type_sequence", "year_specific_sequence")) {
    sq <- if (v == "song_type_sequence") z$seq_song_type else z$seq_year
    write_fasta(z$taxon, sq, file.path(out_dir, v, paste0("song_seqs_", set, "_", i, ".fa")))
    write_fasta(z$taxon, to_prank(sq), file.path(out_dir, v, paste0("song_seqs_", set, "_", i, "_prank.fa")))
    n_files <- n_files + 2
  }
}

# number of taxa per set
n_tax <- function(set, lek) { f <- file.path(out_dir, "song_type_sequence", paste0("song_seqs_", set, "_", lek, ".fa")); if (file.exists(f)) sum(grepl("^>", readLines(f))) else 0 }
check <- expand.grid(lek = sel_leks, set = names(sets), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
check$taxa <- mapply(n_tax, check$set, check$lek)
xtabs(taxa ~ lek + set, check)

data.frame(fasta_files = n_files, taxa = nrow(yrs), taxa_with_recording_that_year = sum(yrs$has_recording),
           taxa_using_representative_sequence = sum(!yrs$has_recording))

```

# Evaluation

## Similarity between copies of the same song type

Similarity between two sequences is 1 - edit distance / length of the longer sequence. The baseline is the similarity between recordings of different song types from the same lek.

```{r similarity}

same <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(rec$ID, rec$lek.song.type), function(z) if (length(z) > 1) t(combn(z, 2)) else NULL))
same_sim <- apply(same, 1, function(p) similarity(p[1], p[2]))

set.seed(1)
diff_pairs <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(rec, rec$lek), function(z) {
  if (length(unique(z$lek.song.type)) < 2) return(NULL)
  p <- t(combn(seq_len(nrow(z)), 2)); p <- p[z$lek.song.type[p[, 1]] != z$lek.song.type[p[, 2]], , drop = FALSE]
  p <- p[sample(nrow(p), min(300, nrow(p))), , drop = FALSE]
  cbind(z$ID[p[, 1]], z$ID[p[, 2]])
}))
diff_sim <- apply(diff_pairs, 1, function(p) similarity(p[1], p[2]))

fs <- list.files("./data/processed/fossils", pattern = "taxa_.*\\.tsv$", full.names = TRUE)
rb_taxa <- unique(unlist(lapply(fs, function(f) read.delim(f)[[1]])))
rb_types <- unique(sub("-[0-9]{4}$", "", rb_taxa))

data.frame(comparison = c("same song type", "different song types, same lek"),
           pairs = c(length(same_sim), length(diff_sim)),
           mean = round(c(mean(same_sim), mean(diff_sim)), 3),
           q25 = round(c(quantile(same_sim, .25), quantile(diff_sim, .25)), 3),
           median = round(c(median(same_sim), median(diff_sim)), 3),
           q75 = round(c(quantile(same_sim, .75), quantile(diff_sim, .75)), 3))

data.frame(chance_corrected_similarity = round((mean(same_sim) - mean(diff_sim)) / (1 - mean(diff_sim)), 3),
           same_type_pairs_above_median_different_type = round(mean(same_sim > median(diff_sim)), 3))

```

```{r similarity plot, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}

ggplot(data.frame(similarity = c(same_sim, diff_sim),
                  comparison = rep(c("same song type", "different song types, same lek"), c(length(same_sim), length(diff_sim)))),
       aes(similarity, fill = comparison)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.6) + scale_fill_viridis_d(end = 0.8, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Similarity between recordings", y = "Density") + theme(legend.position = "top")

```

## Agreement of the broad sections between copies of the same song type

Two comparisons between all pairs of recordings of the same song type, using only the broad category of each segment: similarity of the 5 ms sequences (edit distance, as sequences differ in length) and position-by-position agreement after splitting each song into 20 equal-length parts.

```{r broad agreement between copies}

broad <- function(z) ifelse(z %in% c("F", "S"), "T", "N")
kappa <- function(a, b) {
  lv <- union(a, b); cm <- table(factor(a, lv), factor(b, lv))
  acc <- sum(diag(cm)) / sum(cm); pe <- sum(rowSums(cm) * colSums(cm)) / sum(cm)^2
  (acc - pe) / (1 - pe)
}

# 5 ms sequences
broad_str <- sapply(Q, function(z) paste(broad(z), collapse = ""))
broad_sim <- function(p) 1 - adist(broad_str[[p[1]]], broad_str[[p[2]]])[1, 1] / max(nchar(broad_str[[p[1]]]), nchar(broad_str[[p[2]]]))
same_broad <- apply(same, 1, broad_sim); diff_broad <- apply(diff_pairs, 1, broad_sim)

# 20 equal-length parts: broad category of the section covering most of each part
parts20 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(rec$ID, function(id) {
  ii <- which(segs$ID == id); k <- CT[[id]]; b <- seq(k$start, k$end, length.out = 21)
  data.frame(ID = id, segment = 1:20,
             broad = segs$class[sapply(1:20, function(j) ii[which.max(pmax(0, pmin(segs$end[ii], b[j + 1]) - pmax(segs$start[ii], b[j])))])])
}))
B20 <- split(parts20$broad, parts20$ID)
a20 <- unlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(same)), function(i) B20[[same[i, 1]]]))
b20 <- unlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(same)), function(i) B20[[same[i, 2]]]))
d_a20 <- unlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(diff_pairs)), function(i) B20[[diff_pairs[i, 1]]]))
d_b20 <- unlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(diff_pairs)), function(i) B20[[diff_pairs[i, 2]]]))
pair_agree20 <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(same)), function(i) mean(B20[[same[i, 1]]] == B20[[same[i, 2]]]))

data.frame(measure = c("5 ms sequences, similarity", "20 equal-length parts, position by position"),
           pairs = nrow(same),
           same_song_type = round(c(mean(same_broad), mean(a20 == b20)), 3),
           q25 = round(c(quantile(same_broad, .25), quantile(pair_agree20, .25)), 3),
           median = round(c(median(same_broad), median(pair_agree20)), 3),
           q75 = round(c(quantile(same_broad, .75), quantile(pair_agree20, .75)), 3),
           different_song_types_same_lek = round(c(mean(diff_broad), mean(d_a20 == d_b20)), 3),
           kappa = c(NA, round(kappa(a20, b20), 3)))

```


# Output files

All files are saved in `data/processed`. The evaluation and the spectrograms in this report use the five leks.

| Output | Five leks used in the paper (`r nrow(rec)` recordings, `r nrow(by_type)` song types) | All leks (`r summary_all$recordings` recordings, `r summary_all$song_types` song types) |
|:-----|:-----|:-----|
| Segments | `song_5ms_segments_by_recording.csv` | `song_5ms_segments_by_recording_all_leks.csv` |
| Sequence per song type and year | `song_5ms_sequences_by_taxon.csv` | `song_5ms_sequences_by_taxon_all_leks.csv` |
| One sequence per song type | `song_5ms_sequences_by_song_type.csv` | `song_5ms_sequences_by_song_type_all_leks.csv` |
| FASTA of all recordings | `song_sequences_5ms/all_recordings.fa` | `song_sequences_5ms/all_recordings_all_leks.fa` |
| FASTA files for alignment | `song_sequences_5ms/song_type_sequence/` and `song_sequences_5ms/year_specific_sequence/` | not available |

# Spectrograms of all recordings {#sec-spectrograms}

All recordings of the `r length(rb_types)` song types used in the RevBayes analyses, with one tab per lek and grouped by song type within each tab. Each panel shows the spectrogram with the 5 ms states overlaid and the tailored contour (orange). The strips on top show the classified sections (steps 1 and 2) and the final 5 ms states (steps 3 and 4). All spectrograms in this report have the same time range (`r time_range_ms` ms), so segments have the same size in all of them.

```{r spectrograms, fig.width = 10.5, fig.height = 4, results = "asis"}

show <- rec[rec$lek.song.type %in% rb_types, ]
show <- show[order(show$lek.song.type, show$year), ]

cat("\n\n::: {.panel-tabset}\n\n")
for (lk in unique(show$lek)) {
  cat("\n\n## ", lk, "\n\n", sep = "")
  for (ty in unique(show$lek.song.type[show$lek == lk])) {
    cat("\n\n### ", ty, " {.unnumbered}\n\n", sep = "")
    for (id in show$ID[show$lek.song.type == ty]) {
      plot_step(id, c(2, 4))
      cat("\n\n")
    }
  }
}
cat("\n\n:::\n\n")

```

<div class="alert alert-success">

# Takeaways {.unnumbered .unlisted}

- `r nrow(rec)` recordings of `r nrow(by_type)` song types were coded as sequences of `r segment_ms` ms segments (median length `r median(rec$length)`, range `r min(rec$length)` - `r max(rec$length)`) with 5 states: fast and slow trills (< `r trill_cut_ms` ms and ≥ `r trill_cut_ms` ms trill period, measured over each trill section) and descending, flat and ascending tones (slope thresholds of ±`r tone_cut` kHz/s, measured per segment in a `r 2 * tone_window_ms + segment_ms` ms window)
- Copies of the same song type have a mean similarity of `r sprintf("%.3f", mean(same_sim))`, compared with `r sprintf("%.3f", mean(diff_sim))` for different song types from the same lek
- For the broad categories alone, copies of the same song type have a mean similarity of `r sprintf("%.3f", mean(same_broad))` (`r sprintf("%.3f", mean(diff_broad))` for different song types from the same lek)
- Sequences cover all `r length(rb_types)` song types used in the RevBayes analyses

</div>
